subtype: Approach: planning only the fun parts and ignoring food and time [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Ishita. For my tenth birthday I planned five games: musical chairs, pass the parcel, a treasure trail, a balloon race and dumb charades. I wrote them on a card and felt very organised. I did not write when the cake would be cut, or who would eat what. On the day, nobody had eaten since lunch, and by five o'clock two friends were sitting on the stairs with sad faces. The charades had not even started when the doorbell rang and parents began arriving. Jomon's mother waited at the door with her scooter keys. My party ended with half the games unplayed and me feeling terrible.

qa.q: How many games did Ishita plan?
How did Ishita feel when the party ended with half the games unplayed?
qa.a: Ishita felt terrible and probably disappointed, since the plan looked good on the card but did not work on the day.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Ishita use next time, and why?
qa.a: Ishita could write a time for each activity and put snacks in the plan, because a schedule shows if the games fit before parents come. Ishita could ask a parent to look over the plan.

qa.q: How might Jomon's mother see the party running late?
qa.a: Jomon's mother waited at the door with scooter keys, so the delay probably felt inconvenient and worrying, especially if the parent did not know how long the games would take.

grounding: A girl plans five games but forgets snacks and timings, so the guests are hungry and the games run past pick-up time.

subtype: Approach: planning only the fun parts and ignoring food and time [Pitfall]
passage: For next year, written after Lalremsiami's party, Saturday. She planned five games herself, and they were good ones: sack race, treasure hunt, dumb charades, a quiz, musical chairs. But the plan had no snacks and no times. By 5 pm the children were hungry and cranky; Abhinav was lying on the floor saying he was starving. I sent out for samosas, but the treasure hunt was still going at 6:30 when parents started ringing the bell. Two families left before the cake was cut. Lalremsiami cried in her room afterwards. Next year I'll sit with her and we'll put times and food on the list first.

qa.q: What time did parents start ringing the bell?
qa.a: At 6:30, while the treasure hunt was still going.

qa.q: How did Lalremsiami feel after the party?
qa.a: She cried in her room, so she felt hurt and disappointed that families left before the cake and the day went wrong.

qa.q: What would you add first to Lalremsiami's plan next year?
qa.a: A snack time and a rough length for each game, so guests are fed and the cake happens before pickup.

qa.q: What was the party like for Abhinav?
qa.a: Abhinav was so hungry by 5 pm that he lay on the floor saying he was starving, so the games stopped being fun for him.

grounding: Shows a girl who planned five games but no snacks or timings, so guests got hungry at 5 pm and games ran past pickup time.

subtype: Approach: planning only the fun parts and ignoring food and time [Pitfall]
passage:
Sunday night
My party was today and I'm not happy. I planned everything fun: five games, prizes, a dance at the end. I didn't plan food except the cake, and I didn't think about how long anything would take. At five, Deepak asked, 'Is there anything to eat?' and then everyone was asking. Ammi ran to make pakoras, and the kitchen filled with smoke. The treasure hunt took an hour instead of twenty minutes, so we never did the dance. Then the parents came and waited in the doorway while we were still finding clues. Ammi said, 'Afreen beti, next time, snacks and a clock.' She's right.

qa.q: How long did the treasure hunt take?
qa.a: An hour instead of twenty minutes.

qa.q: How does Afreen feel about the day?
qa.a: Afreen feels unhappy and disappointed, because the fun she planned was spoiled by hunger and running out of time.

qa.q: What could Afreen try when planning her next party?
qa.a: Write a time next to each game and put snacks at a set point, like 'five o'clock: pakoras'; planning only the fun parts left gaps.

qa.q: How might the party have felt for the parents waiting in the doorway?
qa.a: They came at pickup time and had to stand waiting while clues were still being found, which may have been awkward and tiring.

grounding: Illustrates a girl planning only the games of her party, forgetting food and timings, so guests grow hungry and games overrun pickup.
